messages:
nate: Observed authz flip-flop on canary. Same API key -> success then 403 within ~30s. Happened 3x in last hour. Repro below. :thinking:

nate: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" -H "X-Route-ID: embeddings-prod" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -> 200
nate: repeat same curl -> 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope"} 

nate: Logs snippet:```
2026-03-18T15:12:21Z authz=pass api_key=ak_123 route=embeddings keytag=rt-2026-03
2026-03-18T15:12:51Z authz=deny api_key=ak_123 route=embeddings reason=scope_mismatch cached_scope=chat-only
```

olivia: :eyes: Can you paste the token metadata from KMS and authz cache dump? suspecting stale cache after rewrap/rotation.

nate: Pasted small extract to thread: ```kms_tags: ["model:embed-v2", "route:embeddings-prod"]
authz_cache[ak_123]: scope=embed:read version=42 last_checked=2026-03-18T15:10Z
```

maria: Timeline question — any recent canary that flipped the per-route allowlist enforcement flag? We landed a patch yesterday to introduce a permissive fallback for legacy tokens.

devon: I rolled the canary 2h ago that toggles `enable_per_route_enforce` true|false based on traffic. It might be using an old feature-flag value for some nodes.

leo: Hypothesis: on some workers the authz decision engine reads route metadata from service discovery, on others it reads from KMS tags at request time. If the canary changed which source is authoritative, tokens with model-scoped tags can be considered chat-only during a transient config mix.

olivia: Repro plan: 1) force a key rotation (kms rewrap) for a test token 2) run rapid requests hitting different canary buckets 3) dump authz_cache and route metadata simultaneously. Anyone on-call can run?

nate: Running a controlled rewrap on staging now. Will post results.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-015 authz-flipflop-canary, severity=P2, owner=olivia.

olivia: Observed mismatch during rewrap: KMS returned new tag set immediately but authz cache retained old `scope=chat-only` for 25s. Some requests routed to nodes with freshly reloaded KMS tags -> allowed; some kept using stale cache -> denied.

maria: That aligns. We also have a batching optimization that memoizes scope decisions keyed by (api_key, route_hash) but doesn't invalidate on keytag updates. Bug.

devon: Short-term mitigation: make canary rollback to previous enforcement behavior (permissive fallback) and add cache invalidation hook on KMS rewrap event. I can push rollback in 15m.

leo: Also suggest emergency authz cache eviction endpoint: POST /internal/admin/evict-authz?api_key=ak_123 — runable by oncall.

olivia: Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/4621 — adds KMS-watcher -> publish authz.invalidate(api_key) on tag change; adds metric authz.cache_miss_on_rewrap.

nate: After rollback + evict we saw no more 403s for same key in next 30m. Mitigation working. :thumbsup:

maria: Next actions: 1) backport fix to prod branch 2) add unit/integration tests for rewrap -> authz eviction 3) audit logs change: include kms_tag_version in authz decision log.

devon: On-call note: we should also add detection alert: rate of immediate successive authz.pass->deny for same api_key > 5/min -> automates canary pause.

leo: Vulnerability triage: is this exploitable? It’s a denial-of-service-ish regression (could cause app-level errors). Not an elevation of privilege. Severity remains Medium.

olivia: I've scheduled a short postmortem sync tomorrow @10am. Will attach timeline, root cause, and follow-up owners.

nate: Thanks everyone. I'll link the incident logs + traces in the PM doc.

sre-bot: INC-2026-015 updated: status=mitigated, mitigated_by=devon, notes=rollback+evict, next=deploy_fix-prod.
